title: HLA-B*5701 / abacavir hypersensitivity: actionable pharmacogenomic positive control
summary: Positive-control record for MKH-PAT-0015 and for the clinical-actionability side of genomics. It shows a gene-drug relation where screening, avoidance, and guideline implementation are explicitly encoded.

status_history.note: Promoted to prevent candidate-gene denominator pattern from erasing high-actionability pharmacogenomic successes.

place.scope: abacavir prescribing and hypersensitivity-risk management; not generalized to all pharmacogenomics

claims.claim: NIH ClinicalInfo recommends screening for HLA-B*5701 before starting abacavir-containing regimens, recommends that HLA-B*5701-positive patients not be prescribed abacavir, and says positive status should be recorded as an abacavir allergy.
what_would_change_status: The guideline is superseded or changes the screening/no-prescription recommendation.

claims.claim: The NIH page summarizes PREDICT-1 as a randomized prospective-screening study in which HLA-B*5701 screening eliminated immunologically confirmed abacavir hypersensitivity compared with standard care (0% vs 2.7%) and lowered clinically suspected hypersensitivity (3.4% vs 7.8%).
what_would_change_status: A corrected guideline or trial report changes the PREDICT-1 outcome numbers or design description.

claims.claim: The record retains clinical-judgment limits: NIH notes lower specificity and says HLA-B*5701 should not substitute for clinical judgment or pharmacovigilance, because a negative result does not absolutely rule out every form of abacavir hypersensitivity.
what_would_change_status: A revised guideline states that HLA-B*5701 testing fully replaces clinical monitoring or materially changes the specificity/negative-result cautions.

evidence_profile.effect_type: gene-drug adverse-reaction risk with screening/avoidance intervention

type_payload.fit_rationale: A high-actionability pharmacogenomic example with guideline-backed screening and bounded limits.
limits: Predominantly abacavir/HLA-B*5701-specific; not generalizable to all gene-drug pairs.
Guideline date and current ARV practice need periodic review.
Clinical management remains necessary despite screening.

handling_notes: Genetic findings must not be represented as deterministic individual destiny.
No clinical advice, testing advice, or individual-level participant data is encoded.
Population/ancestry, phenotype, and actionability scope must remain visible.

unknowns: Whether the cube should create a dedicated pharmacogenomics actionability sublane.
Whether current guideline updates after the archived section have changed operational details.
next_actions: Add CPIC guideline source with exact page locators if accessible.
Add a pharmacogenomics negative-control case where promising association did not achieve actionability.

scope_qualifiers.ancestry_or_population_scope: source/guideline scope not universalized beyond drug relation
scope_qualifiers.portability_caution: do not generalize to all HLA/drug relations
